---
title: "How to leave out the insertions the QC flags"
---

Some IBL insertions should not be used to train or evaluate a model: the probe is not where
its alignment places it, or a band of the recording is broken. `ephysatlas.qc` checks every
insertion of a feature release automatically and labels it per component. The labels ship
with the package as `ephysatlas.fixtures.pid_qc_filter`; reading them needs no account and
no data.

## The labels

Each insertion gets one label per component, `good`, `review` or `bad`:

| Component | Bad when |
|---|---|
| `alignment` | the recording is more typical somewhere else (another depth along the probe, the other probe's track in a two-probe session), or both its LF and its spike band are unusual for where it is placed |
| `lf` | the LF band alone is unusual for where the probe is placed, or its signal is unusual anywhere |
| `ap` | the AP band (not the LF) is unusual for where the probe is placed, or its signal is unusual anywhere, including a fifth of the channels dead or noisy |
| `waveform` | the AP band is bad, the waveforms are unusual anywhere, or the spike band (not the LF) is unusual for where the probe is placed |

*Unusual for where the probe is placed* compares the recording with what the other probes
record within 300 µm of the same positions, never with a model's prediction. Only the data
decide: no model, no auto-alignment and no manual label enters the QC.

```python
from ephysatlas.fixtures import pid_qc_filter

pid_qc_filter.VINTAGE, pid_qc_filter.LEVEL   # ('2026_W42', 'L3')
pid_qc_filter.qc_labels("0228bcfd-632e-49bd-acd4-c334cf9213e9")
# {'alignment': 'bad', 'lf': 'good', 'ap': 'bad', 'waveform': 'bad',
#  'checks': 'wf_outlier;ap_signal;depth;swap'}
```

`checks` lists the failure cases that fired; their definitions are
`ephysatlas.qc.levels.TESTS`. Unlisted insertions are good on every component.

## Leave them out of a dataset

`excluded_pids` returns the insertions bad on any of the components you name:

```python
from ephysatlas.fixtures import pid_qc_filter

channel_bad = pid_qc_filter.excluded_pids()   # any component: 175 of 1,049 for 2026_W42
unit_bad = pid_qc_filter.excluded_pids(("alignment", "ap", "waveform"))   # 147
cautious = pid_qc_filter.excluded_pids(include_review=True)   # also those to review: 244
```

Pass the list as `exclude_pids` to the loaders:

```python
from ephysatlas.spatial_encoder.utils import LoadInsertionData

pids, features, xyz, planned_xyz = LoadInsertionData(
    VINTAGE="2026_W42", exclude_pids=pid_qc_filter.excluded_pids()
)
```

`alignment.ChannelDataset.load` and
`unit_level_encoder.prepare_data.prepare_latest_cells_encoder_data` take the same argument.

::: {.callout-note}
## The default

Without `exclude_pids`, the channel loaders leave out the insertions bad on any component,
`excluded_pids()`, and the unit loader those bad for their alignment, AP band or waveforms,
`excluded_pids(("alignment", "ap", "waveform"))`. The models released from `2026_W44` on are
trained this way; `ephysatlas.fixtures.misaligned_pids`, the hand-curated list of earlier
releases, is kept for reference only. An empty list keeps every insertion.
:::

## Levels

The QC has five nested levels of sensitivity, from L1 (one failure case beyond 3 robust SDs;
3.5% of the 2026_W42 insertions bad) to L5 (one beyond 2.5 SDs, or two beyond 1 SD; 33%). The
fixture is written at **L3**: an insertion is bad when one failure case is beyond 2.5 robust SDs
or two are beyond 1.5 (17% of the insertions), and *review* when it is bad only at L4 (two
beyond 1.25). Retraining the channel-level model without the insertions bad at each level
changed its held-out accuracy by no more than the variability between trainings at any level;
L3 catches more of the problems planted in random insertions than L2 at no measurable cost.

To rebuild the filter, or write it at another level (the measurements are cached, and only
the last stage runs):

```bash
python scripts/build_pid_qc_filter.py --stages levels --level L3 --write-fixture
```

The first run measures every insertion of the release (hours). It needs the release's
features only, and Alyx once for the session of each insertion; see the script's docstring.
